Working-capital days rose from 112 to 130 between FY26 and H1 FY27.

Revenue guidance of ≥ 10% for FY27: The number wasn't repeated on the Q2 FY27 call; management described it only in words. FY27 is still open. H1 FY27 actual +5.9% against ≥ 10%. The rest of FY27 needs +13.9%.
EBITDA margin guidance of 24–25% for FY27: Not repeated on the Q2 FY27 call. FY27 is still open. H1 FY27 actual 23.3% against 24–25%. The rest of FY27 needs 24.7%.
Revenue (US generics) guidance of 15–18% for FY27: Not repeated on the Q2 FY27 call. FY27 is still open. H1 FY27 actual +3.5% against 15–18%. The rest of FY27 needs +13.9%.
Management described net debt in Q2 FY27 in a way the reported figures don't support. Checked against reported figures (change: ₹325.0 cr).

bull_bear.note: Rule-based: each point is a fixed test over the cited facts, and every number in it comes from those facts. A side with nothing listed means no rule fired on the evidence available, not that there is nothing to say.

rules.no_score: FINN doesn't combine these indicators into a trust score: any weighting would be a judgement, not a measurement.

indicators.title: Guidance delivery
indicators.question: When management gave a number, did the reported figure land within it?
indicators.headline: Kept 4 of 4 explicit targets whose period has closed (FY25–FY26).
indicators.method: Closed explicit targets only. Kept = delivered or ahead; the ledger's tolerance applies. A rate needs at least 4 targets across 2 fiscal years.

indicators.title: Where results landed in the range
indicators.question: Does management guide conservatively, or tend to land short of the middle?
indicators.headline: Against the midpoint of the stated range, closed targets landed on the favourable side once, near it twice and on the adverse side once.
indicators.method: Ranges and 'around' figures only. Offset = actual - midpoint, in percentage points for growth and margins, and as a share of the midpoint for amounts. 'Favourable' depends on the metric: above the midpoint for growth, margins and capex; below it for credit cost and debt. Within 0.15 pp or 2% counts as at the midpoint. Counts are shown only from 4 targets across 2 years.

indicators.title: Guidance revisions
indicators.question: How often were targets changed mid-period, and in which direction?
indicators.headline: None of the 8 explicit targets was changed after it was first stated.
indicators.method: A revision is a later statement with a different number for the same metric and period. 'Against the company' means lowered for growth, margins and capex, raised for credit cost and debt. Two documents disagreeing in the same quarter are reported as a contradiction, not counted as a revision.

indicators.title: Capex execution
indicators.question: Did the company spend what it said it would?
indicators.headline: Capex was guided, but no guided year has closed yet.
indicators.method: Capex = purchase of property, plant and equipment in the cash flow statement (year-end filing). The plan is the first figure stated for the year, so mid-year cuts don't hide under-spending.

indicators.title: Revenue growth against what was guided
indicators.question: How did revenue growth compare with what management said to expect?
indicators.headline: 2 of 2 closed explicit revenue targets kept.
indicators.method: Each statement is shown with the reported figure for its period. Constant-currency and worded statements are listed but not scored.

indicators.title: Margin progression
indicators.question: Did margins move the way management said they would?
indicators.headline: 2 of 2 closed explicit margin targets kept.
indicators.method: Each statement is shown with the reported figure for its period. Constant-currency and worded statements are listed but not scored.

indicators.title: Cash generation against profit
indicators.question: Does reported profit turn into cash, and does management describe it fairly?
indicators.headline: Operating cash flow was 77%–81% of EBITDA across FY24–FY26.
indicators.method: Full years from the year-end cash flow statement. What management said about cash is set against the ratio for the same period.

indicators.title: Targets that went quiet
indicators.question: Does management stop mentioning targets it is going to miss?
indicators.headline: 4 explicit targets went quiet (not repeated, withdrawn or restated in words) without being met.
indicators.method: A target goes quiet when a later complete call transcript doesn't mention it before its period ends, when it is withdrawn, or when the number is restated only in words.

indicators.title: Figures quoted on calls
indicators.question: When management describes a reported quarter, do the statements agree?
indicators.headline: 5 of 6 figures management quoted about reported periods match the statements; 1 contradicted.
indicators.method: Checked on every plausible basis (year on year, sequential, level) before a figure is called contradicted.

interpretation.text: Management kept 4 of 4 explicit targets whose period has closed (FY25–FY26).
The record on closed targets is good, but 3 of 4 current targets are behind on the latest reported figures; the record alone isn't a reason to trust this year's numbers.

contradictions.text: Management described net debt in Q2 FY27 in a way the reported figures don't support. Checked against reported figures (change: ₹325.0 cr).
contradictions.implication: Treat management's characterisation of this quarter with caution; ask which basis they used.

contradictions.text: For FY27 EBITDA margin, the Q4 FY26 presentation said 24.5–25.5% and the transcript said 24–25%.
contradictions.implication: Two company documents for the same quarter disagree on the target. FINN tracks the later one; ask which the company stands by.
